title: Desk-test verdicts
description: The verdict each payload of a desk-test set must get on one lock: payloads that someone outside this repository wrote to test the lock's text, kept beside this file in `desk-tests/<set>/`. A payload with a finding is rejected at that location, and only there, by the schemas and rules, by the lock's own checker, and by each SDK the lock's schemas generate, except where an SDK gap records a rule's finding that no SDK type checks; every other payload passes every engine. The desk-tests gate fails on any other verdict, on an undecided check or an SDK gap not recorded here, and on a recorded one that no longer holds.

lock.description: The lock whose text the payloads test, by name.

document.description: The model document every payload is, such as `LineItem`.

checker.description: The lock's own checker: the path of a script the lock pins under `scripts`, run from the root of a tree that holds the lock's specification, its examples with the payloads added, and its scripts.

examples.description: Every payload of the set, by file name in this folder.

findings.description: The payloads that must be rejected, each at one location.

undecided.description: The rules' checks that a payload's values can't decide, because the verdict turns on what the payload leaves out, as for an example.

sdk_gaps.description: The findings the SDKs don't make: each is a rule's, which no SDK type checks, since the types check what the schemas check (type rules § 9), so each SDK accepts the payload there, as the schema does.

path.description: The JSON pointer of the location both engines reject, `""` for the whole payload. The checker reports a key its table doesn't list at the key's object, which the gate reads as the key's own location, as the schemas report it.

kind.description: How the schemas and rules reject it, as an example finding's kind: `load`, `invalid`, `undefined_key`, or `rule`, with the rule it breaks.

rule.description: The rule a `rule` finding breaks, as rules.json names it.

reason.description: Why the payload is rejected there, with the section or issue that says so, in one or two sentences.

path.description: The JSON pointer of the value the rule reads, `""` for the whole payload.

reason.description: What the verdict turns on that the payload leaves out.

path.description: The JSON pointer of the rule's finding, as `findings` records it.

reason.description: Why no SDK makes the finding: what the rule checks that no schema states.
